For millions of people, its reliance on interest (riba) creates a barrier to managing money and building wealth without compromising their values. At Wahed, we're changing that. Mercury is building a complete finance stack for startups. Since we launched Mercury in 2019, our customer base has grown to over 300,000 startups and small businesses from all around the world. With growth comes the need to ensure our customer experience is top of mind even in the most challenging scenarios.

We’re working to build something like magic for a really wide range of startup businesses. A key piece of the magic we’ve built thus far has been smart, product-driven support, and we’re looking to bring on an operational-focused, thoughtful Support Manager to help us continuously improve our Risk Support experience as we scale quickly.

You’ll join as the second manager on our Risk Support team, partnering closely with an existing Risk Support Manager to execute the operational function of the team and support the wider strategic vision. You’ll manage your own cohort of specialists who are dedicated to managing customer interactions and operational tasks across key risk-related workstreams. You’ll collaborate with multiple Risk teams at Mercury, including AML, Fraud, ODD, Onboarding, Sanctions, and Risk UX, to provide clear, thoughtful, and accurate support systems to help customers impacted by risk-related decisions or processes.

Beyond your own team, you’ll help run a growing Risk Support operation: scoping and executing our BPO partnership strategy for Risk Support, and expanding newer programs like proactive outreach and VIP/managed support. • A strong familiarity or expertise supporting KYC, KYB, AML processes and other regulatory requirements

• A collaborative leadership style and comfort sharing ownership of a function with a peer manager

• Previous experience partnering cross-functionally with engineering, product, risk, and compliance teams

• Consistent empathy while helping entrepreneurs build successful businesses

Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.

Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech

Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.

We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors,  you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

International payments is complex, competitive, and evolving fast. You will craft positioning that resonates with merchants, drive high-impact launches, arm the sales team with competitive assets, and more. This is a high-visibility, cross-functional role where marketing, product, sales, and compliance intersect.

This role sits at the heart of how our international payments products go to market.

  • Own GTM for key launches end‑to‑end – customer and market insight, positioning, launch strategy, and post‑launch adoption

  • Partner with Product and Growth to identify opportunities across merchant cohorts, payment methods, and use cases

The Information Security organization advances the overall state of security at Rubrik through critical initiatives and coordination of large security projects. Information Security builds technologies, tools, and processes to better enable teams at Rubrik to develop secure software and protect data and systems with appropriate security controls. Information Security also develops systems to monitor and respond to attacks against our assets, provides awareness education to teams on security best practices for data protection, and ensures data governance and data sharing relationships with third parties in order to securely protect Rubrik information. 

 

About the role:

We are looking for a Manager, CyberSecurity Risk Management to join our security risk management team and support the delivery of Rubrik's cybersecurity risk management program. Working closely with the team's lead Program Manager, who owns the program, you will help drive day-to-day execution: coordinating cross-functional risk assessments, supporting risk review and acceptance processes, tracking risk remediation to closure, and producing risk reporting that gives leadership a clear view of Rubrik's cybersecurity risk posture. You will partner with Security, Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, Procurement, and Finance to keep work on track and deliver measurable outcomes. Success in this role requires strong program management discipline, solid risk and compliance knowledge, and the ability to influence and build consensus at every level of the company.

What you’ll do:

  • Support program operations for the overall Cybersecurity Risk Management Program.
  • Support and conduct risk assessments and triage incoming security issues related to Rubrik’s core products, services, and infrastructure. 
  • Draft clear risk statements that translate technical findings into business impact, including likelihood/impact rationale and key assumptions. 
  • Maintain and update the risk register, ensuring ownership, status, target dates, and risk treatment decisions are accurate and timely.
  • Coordinate and track cross-functional risk initiatives, managing timelines, dependencies, and action items; flag delivery risks early and drive follow-through.
  • Drive remediation of risks to closure by conducting periodic cross-functional check-ins with risk owners to obtain updates, track milestones and target dates, document progress in the risk register, remove/escalate blockers, and communicate status through leadership reporting. 
  • Support the risk governance cadence, including preparing materials for risk committee meetings, facilitating risk acceptance and exception reviews, and tracking escalations, decisions, and actions to completion.
  • Collect and analyze program metrics (KPIs/KRIs), build dashboards, and help prepare risk updates for leadership.
  • Support the risk assessment program at scale, including enterprise, technical, and third-party/supplier risk assessments, helping keep methodology, quality, and turnaround times consistent.
  • Execute and document cybersecurity risk assessments (inherent and residual) for systems, applications, cloud services, and initiatives; gather evidence and validate control implementation with stakeholders.
  • Help map program activities to compliance obligations and frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF/800-53, PCI DSS, HIPAA) and emerging regulations (e.g., DORA, NIS2, EU AI Act).
  • Contribute to risk quantification efforts so risks can be prioritized in business and financial terms.
  • Support GRC tooling, automation, and AI-enabled improvement initiatives by gathering requirements, coordinating implementation tasks, piloting use cases (e.g., LLM-assisted intake triage, evidence mapping, and automated status summarization), and driving adoption of standardized workflows with appropriate governance and human review.
  • Identify gaps and recommend process improvements to make risk management activities more efficient, consistent, and effective.

Experience you'll need:

  •     8+ years of experience in cybersecurity risk management, or GRC, including at least 3 years in a program or project management role.
  •     Experience supporting or helping scale a cybersecurity risk management program in a fast-paced technology, SaaS, or cloud company.
  •     Strong program management skills: project planning, dependency management, effort estimation, status reporting, and delivery of cross-functional initiatives.
  •     Solid working knowledge of risk management methodologies (NIST RMF / 800-37 / 800-30, ISO 27005, COBIT) and common security frameworks such as ISO 27001/2, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF / 800-53, CIS Controls, PCI DSS, and HIPAA.
  •     Enough technical understanding of cloud, identity, network, and application security to engage credibly with engineering teams and follow remediation plans.
  •     Able to communicate risk clearly to senior stakeholders and build consensus without direct authority.
  •     Hands-on experience with agile project management and reporting tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Tableau).
  •     Excellent written and verbal communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills.
  •     Bachelor's degree in Security, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

About CircuitHub
CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.
We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.
The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.
The Role
CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.
These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:
• 
They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.
• 
They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.
• 
They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.
• 
They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.
• 
They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.
What you'll do
Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.
How we build
• 
Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.
• 
Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change.
• 
Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters.
• 
Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice.
Recent work
• 
Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked.
• 
A photo check for stray parts in robot storage scored 10 out of 10 blind, at about 8¢ a photo. The model it replaced caught about half.
• 
Agent tool calls leave durable receipts, so a session killed mid-deploy resumes without sending the same email or order twice.
• 
Invoices extracted from supplier emails matched what a person had entered 66 times out of 66.
• 
A constraint solver replans the whole factory every two minutes, across robots, ovens and people.
What we look for
• 
You've put LLM agents into production and can tell us what broke and how you knew it was working.
• 
You're a strong software engineer first. Most of this job is real engineering, not prompting: concurrency, idempotency, data modelling, security.
• 
You build the eval before you trust the result.
• 
You like the physical world: cameras, robots, parts rotated by 90°.
• 
Bonus: computer vision, optimisation or electronics.
Stack
• 
Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Claude and OpenAI APIs, MCP, skills in plain Markdown
• 
Code: TypeScript (Bun, React), Python (FastAPI, Dagster, OpenCV, OR-Tools), PostgreSQL
• 
Infra: Nix and NixOS, Nomad, Terraform, Vault, AWS, Modal sandboxes, OpenTelemetry
